newsitem.title: USA: Dean Witter raises cash in asset allocation.
newsitem.headline: Dean Witter raises cash in asset allocation.

text.p: Dean Witter raised cash in its asset allocation model, citing an uncertain outlook for both stocks and bonds.
Dean Witter chief investment strategist Peter Canelo said the firm lowered its stock allocation to 55 percent from 60 percent and its bond allocation to 20 percent from 25 percent.
He said cash now represents 25 percent of the allocation model, up from 15 percent.
"The problem is this period of uncertainty could be more than just a week," Canelo said. "(The Fed) could conceiveably do something depending on the unemployment figures Friday."

Canelo said recent economic data suggested the Federal Reserve faced little choice but to adopt a tighter monetary policy at or even before its September meeting, a course that has yet to be reflected in the markets.
"The market has not yet priced to handle that kind of hike," he said.
